title: Sentry plugin breaks the EAS Android build
story: Adding the Sentry plugin to app.json broke the cloud Gradle build. CI only runs a JavaScript export, so it stayed green. The fix came from comparing with an earlier working build on a side branch.
entry: Trap. EAS Android build errors in 'Run gradlew' after the Sentry package was added to app.json plugins. The plugin adds a Gradle upload step that needs an auth token. Remove it from plugins. The SDK still autolinks. CI cannot see this.
steps: Opus 4.8 held the failure and the repo. CLAUDE.md had no Sentry rule yet. The decisive fact, that build 14 came from a side branch, was in no window.
'Before retrying a failed build or deploy' fires.
The query is the build log, which reaches a session only when the owner pastes it. The paste is not in the record, and the commit quotes only an error code.
An earlier entry comes back as a candidate or as a lead. Nothing exists for the later version bumps.
One card in the calling window, at most 2,000 characters.
Remove one string from app.json plugins. Nothing to adapt.
The check proves the plugin is present, not that it is the whole cause. The real check is the next EAS build, which fails again on three version bumps. CI stays green.
The second failure escalates with only a lookup id. Opus needs a new pasted log and the build-14 comparison. Neither travels in the brief.
The fix meets the write rule, because a build was burned. The version-bump cause is stored as a separate pin.
A phase-close scan labels a stranded fix 'fix not on main'. The auth-token precondition is an EAS-side secret and can never be probed.

title: Empty env value rejected by eas.json
story: A build profile carried an empty Sentry DSN meant as 'off'. EAS rejects empty env values. Every build failed before starting. CI's JavaScript export never reads eas.json.
entry: Trap. Every eas build fails schema validation: an env value is 'not allowed to be empty'. eas.json carries EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN as an empty string. Remove the keys; unset already means off. To enable Sentry, add the key with a real DSN.
worked: At 08-03 the diff warning fired at the first commit and was right.
steps: At the defect the task was a feature, 'wire the DSN, empty means off', run by Fable. A same-feature Sentry trap was in the window and did not cover this. A cheap model gets the same blind spot.
At 07-20 the failed build triggers. At 08-03 the diff check runs at the first commit. At 07-18 nothing could fire, because no entry existed.
The EAS message names the key and the rule and is short to paste. At 08-03 the query is the diff itself.
At 07-20 an out-of-vocabulary rule turns a Sentry-word tie into a miss. At 08-03 the entry matches on the eas.json env key.
One warning line and one card in the session's window.
Trivial: the value must be non-empty.
At 07-18 the gate cannot see eas.json validity, and the strong model wrote the defect. A cheap output equal to Fable's is equally broken.
The error explains itself. No escalation is in the record.
This is the design's model entry: the data value is the cause, with a control pair present and absent.
At 08-03 the warning fires and is right. It adds nothing measurable over CLAUDE.md, which already carried the rule.

title: Floating base image breaks the Railway build
source: Commits afb7065, 9c561b0; deploy workflow first run
story: A Dockerfile hardcoded the bookworm package line, but the floating python:3.12-slim image moved to trixie. The image build failed and production stayed on the old version.
entry: Trap. Railway image build fails: postgresql-client-17 cannot be installed. The Dockerfile hardcodes the bookworm-pgdg apt line, but python:3.12-slim now follows trixie. Build the line from the image's VERSION_CODENAME. CI does not build this Dockerfile.
steps: The first deploy run failed. The writer believed 'bookworm ships 15', the same picture a cheap model brings from training.
The apt error sits in the Railway build log. The session may reach the Actions log through gh. The Railway log needs a paste.
First time: the store is empty for this. A miss is the right answer.
Nothing is delivered on a miss.
No local check exists. The authoritative check is a re-triggered Railway deploy. The strong model's own output was the defect, so 'equal to the strong model' is not success.
Miss, claim, then escalate with the lookup id only. The receiving Opus must fetch the build log again.
It meets the write rule, because a deploy was burned. The precondition is unprobed and the verdict capped. 'Won't break on the next base-image roll-forward' is a stored prediction about a vendor.
No recurrence. A floating tag moves with no local trace, so the store cannot re-check the entry. The Dockerfile comment carried the lesson at no cost.

title: Staging VM unreachable after a PC reboot
source: Staging rig scripts; commit db6c8fa; session S11 lead
story: After a reboot the Hyper-V switch gets a new address range. The firewall rule allowed ssh only from the old one. The 11-04 entry was half right and spread through three later documents.
entry: Trap (staging rig). After a PC reboot rig.sh start brings the VM up at a new address, then 'ssh did not come up'. The Default Switch gets a new /20 inside 172.16.0.0/12 each boot. The rule must name 172.16.0.0/12.
steps: Sonnet 5.5 held the drills task, the rig scripts and the provision script with its comment in a resumed window.
rig.sh start failed after 5 min 23 s, so 'before retrying a failed deploy' fires.
The command output is local. No paste is needed.
It returns the 11-04 entry, which is half right. The error line is a generic ssh wait failure and fits any reason ssh is down.
The card lands in the main window. The compaction summary kept the subnet fact.
The entry's fix was already applied. Nothing to adapt.

The probe tests for the old defect, finds the old fix and returns 'not applies'. The store then proposes a not-when from the 192.168 values, so it learns 'not this entry' for a recurrence of the entry's own cause.
Sonnet solved it in two turns without escalating.
The 11-04 entry passes the write gate because its control pair flips. Nothing can test the generalisation from two samples, yet it is stored as fact.
The half-right fact spread to three later documents. Repair needs two Opus calls for a two-turn Sonnet fix. Cross-project use is not specified, and on a real host 'both private blocks' is wrong.

title: Queued writes deleted on a non-network error
source: Commit c27bb39; O-08-design.md line 62; O-03-design.md line 7
story: A fix classified errors by status. Later, Railway's edge answered some requests with 4xx text and phones parked or dropped writes for weeks. No session ran. An agent first saw it on 10-31.
entry: A queued write that synced into a non-network error was deleted. A typed ApiError carries the status. 401 pauses the queue. 400, 403, 404, 409 and 422 are definitive: move to a visible failed list. 5xx, 429 and timeouts retry. Bias every ambiguity toward keeping the record.
steps: On 07-03 the task is a real defect in the new queues and the outbox contract is in the window. The premise 'a 404 comes from our server' is in no window.
From about 2026-08 phones park and drop for weeks while no session runs. No trigger exists for a failure that never reaches a window.
Nothing to query during the outage. On 10-31 the only text is the host's 'Application not found', which shares no words with any entry.
The diff check surfaces the outbox contract by its identifiers on the changed lines. It is the right entry for the task as posed.
The card sits in the window of the session doing the work.
Adapting to pings, 'droppable, so drop', is what Opus 4.8 did. The output was equal.
Tests mock a 404. Nothing can test who answers a 404. The equal output carried the same exposure.
No visible failure until 10-31. Then the top tier ran the program directly.
The replacement entry comes from a multi-agent workflow. Its premise is dashboard configuration, outside git and outside any footprint.
The vendor change left no local event, so the entry stayed validated. Reuse spread its premise to queues where a 4xx means drop. Pings from the whole outage are gone.
